Food and Drug Administration
Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research
Summary Minutes
193rd Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee Meeting

                                           June 18, 2026

On June 18, 2026, the 193rd meeting of the Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory
Committee (VRBPAC) convened in open session to discuss and make recommendations on
the safety and effectiveness of MFLUSIVA (Influenza Vaccine, mRNA), manufactured by Moderna
TX Inc., with a requested indication in Biologics License Application STN 125869/0 for the prevention
of influenza disease caused by influenza virus subtypes A and type B represented in the vaccine.

On June 18, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), Dr. Arnold Monto, Acting Chairperson,
called the meeting to order. The DFO, Dr. Cicely Reese, made administrative remarks, conducted
rollcall, invited the VRBPAC members and consultants to introduce themselves, and read the Conflict
of Interest (COI) statement into the public record. There were no conflict-of-interest waivers issued
under 18 U.S. Code Section 208 in connection with this meeting.

Dr. David Kaslow, Office of Vaccines Research and Review, provided the Introduction to the VRBPAC
Meeting Topics, and Dr. Joseph Kulinski provided a brief review of Biologics License Application for
STN 125869/0, followed by Questions and Answers (Q&A).

Following Introductory Remarks and Overview, the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC),
a Guest Speaker on Seasonal Influenza Vaccines, regulated industry and FDA presenters provided
presentations entitled:
• CDC: Seasonal Influenza Vaccine Surveillance and Effectiveness: Lisa Grohskopf, MD, MPH
• Seasonal Influenza Vaccines: Current Status and Opportunities for Improved Effectiveness: Richard
    Webby, PhD
• Moderna Presentations:
        o Moderna Investigational Influenza Vaccine mRNA-1010 in Adults = 50 Years:
            Rituparna Das, MD, PhD
        o Epidemiology of Seasonal Influenza in US Adults =50 Years and Effectiveness of Current
            Vaccines: Evan Anderson, MD, FIDSA, FPIDS
        o Clinical Data: Efficacy and Immunogenicity of mRNA-1010:
            Rituparna Das, MD, PhD
        o Clinical Safety: Eleanor Wilson, MD, MHS
        o Benefit-Risk and Summary: Rituparna Das, MD, PhD
• FDA Presentation: FDA Review of Efficacy, Immunogenicity, and Safety of MFLUSIVA
    (Influenza Vaccine, mRNA) in Adults 50 Years of Age and Older: Gauri Raval, MD, MPH;
    Timothy P. Brennan, MD, PhD, MS

A 40-minute lunch break was held after the FDA presentation.

After the lunch break, Dr. Monto convened the Open Public Hearing (OPH). Four registered speakers
presented remarks during the OPH. The Chairperson closed the session and moved into presentations to
the Committee.

Immediately following the OPH, an additional Q&A session was held for the CDC, Industry, and FDA
Presenters.

Food and Drug Administration

Summary Minutes
193rd Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee Meeting

                                           June 18, 2026

The Chairperson began the general Committee Discussion of the topic. After the general discussion
concluded, the Chairperson and DFO invited and led the Committee into the voting session. The
outcome of the voting questions is noted below:

Voting Question 1: Do the benefits of mFlusiva outweigh its risks for the prevention of influenza
disease in adults 50 through 64 years of age?

The vote was Yes: 9 No: 0 Abstain: 0.

Voting Question 2: Do the benefits of mFlusiva outweigh its risks for the prevention of influenza
disease in adults 65 years of age and older?

The vote was Yes: 9 No: 0 Abstain: 0.

Meeting Summary:

The 193rd VRBPAC meeting, held on 18 June 2026, focused on evaluating the safety and effectiveness of
MFLUSIVA (Influenza Vaccine, mRNA; mRNA-1010), manufactured by Moderna, for the prevention of
influenza disease in adults 50 years of age and older. Committee members broadly supported the benefit-risk
profile of MFLUSIVA. Discussion topics included labeling of the elevated reactogenicity profile, need for the
second season data, establishment of correlates of protection, assessment of cell-mediated immunity and strain
selection framework for mRNA-based influenza vaccines. Members emphasized the need for data in populations
including immunocompromised, frail adults, and pregnant women. The committee voted unanimously 9–0 on
both questions, recommending that the benefits of MFLUSIVA outweigh its risks for adults 50 through 64 years
of age (supporting traditional approval) and for adults 65 years of age and older (supporting accelerated
approval).

Following Committee voting and the summary, Acting Chairperson, Dr. Arnold Monto, invited Dr.
Kaslow to provide closing remarks. Dr. Kaslow thanked the committee for the 193rd VRBPAC
meeting, which discussed the safety and effectiveness of MFLUSIVA (Influenza Vaccine, mRNA),
manufactured by Moderna TX Inc., with a requested indication in Biologics License Application STN
125869/0 for the prevention of influenza disease caused by influenza virus subtypes A and type B
represented in the vaccine.

Following Dr. Kaslow’s closing remarks, the committee DFO adjourned the meeting on June 18, 2026,
at 2:53 p.m. EDT.

Additional meeting information and details can be obtained from the transcript, which can be viewed
at:
2026 Meeting Materials, Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee | FDA.
